title: Permanently erase a deleted custom field
when: The step asks to permanently erase a custom field that was already deleted and is waiting in an object's Deleted Fields list, to free its API name or a field-count slot. It is not deleting a live field, and it is not undeleting one.
steps: In Object Manager, click the object the step names.
In the object's sidebar, click 'Fields & Relationships', then click the 'Deleted Fields' button.
In the row for the named field, click 'Erase'. Click only that one row's Erase.
Salesforce asks for confirmation: tick 'Yes, I want to permanently delete the custom field', then click 'Delete'.
doneWhen: The object's Deleted Fields list no longer shows the named field.

verified.outcome: Trial step matched at p=1.00; 6 actions, 43 s, run with --allow-destructive: Account, Fields & Relationships, Deleted Fields, the row's Erase (p=0.98), the 'Yes, I want to permanently delete' box, Delete. Ended by the Setup Audit Trail: Salesforce recorded 'Permanently deleted custom field Autopilot Trial Field', Jev p=0.95. It failed three times first, none of them a wrong choice: Object Manager draws its content after its sidebar settles, so early looks saw five controls; then a rule meant for saved settings pages reopened the start path in the middle of the confirmation.

notes: The field's data is unrecoverable afterwards, so the run stops for a person unless --allow-destructive is given. The trial needs a custom field deployed and then deleted first. Pure Lightning pages, an embedded Classic list, and a confirmation dialog.

trial.step: Permanently erase the deleted custom field Autopilot Trial Field from the Account object.
